extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, mathematical analysts, and philosophers examining the foundations and methods of calculus (fluxions/differentials)
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing the legitimacy, clarity, and logical soundness of the methods and principles used in modern analysis (fluxions, infinitesimals, differences, and associated notations), with emphasis on whether proofs rest on clear premises and legitimate inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of definitions, postulates, and axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Definitions are clear; when the Postulata cannot be refused, nor the Axioms denied; when from the distinct Contemplation and Comparison of Figures, their Properties are derived by a perpetual well-connected chain of Consequences, the habit of reasoning is close and exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep objects in view and attention fixed; ensure definitions and foundational postulates are explicit and unquestionable before deriving theorems from them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom to examine mathematical principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The Principles and Methods [of mathematicians] to be examined with the same freedom which you assume with regard to the Principles and Mysteries of Religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematical methods (especially modern analysis) must be open to impartial scrutiny; practitioners do not have special immunity from critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear conception of fluxions (what fluxions are)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fluxions are said to be nearly as the Increments of the flowing Quantities generated in the least equal Particles of time; and to be accurately in the first Proportion of the nascent, or in the last of the evanescent, Increments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an unequivocal, intelligible account of what a fluxion denotes (velocity, nascent increment, or other); avoid multiple incompatible descriptions of the same notion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceivability of moments/nascent increments
rubrics_metrics.description: Moments of nascent Increments of flowing Quantities are very difficult to conceive ... it seems more difficult to conceive the abstracted Velocities of such nascent imperfect Entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a method relies on 'moments' (infinitesimal increments), the author must argue that such entities are conceptually coherent or provide a substitute formulation in finite terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence of infinite hierarchies of infinitesimals/differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences of various Orders, i.e. Quantities infinitely less than Quantities infinitely little; and infinitesimal Parts of infinitesimals of infinitesimals, &c. without end or limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods invoking an infinite regress of ever-smaller infinitesimals must justify that such a hierarchy is well-defined and does not produce contradiction or loss of meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of shifting or contradictory suppositions
rubrics_metrics.description: It amounts ... to suppose an Increment is something, derive consequences, then suppose the Increments vanish (are nothing) and yet retain consequences obtained by assuming they were something.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not first assume the existence of nonzero increments to compute expressions and then set them to zero while keeping derived nontrivial terms; arguments must be conducted under a single consistent suppositional framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma on rejected hypotheses and their consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If, by virtue of a supposed Point, certain other Points are attained; and such supposed Point be itself afterwards destroyed or rejected by a contrary Supposition; in that case, all the other Points attained thereby must also be destroyed and rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an initial hypothesis is later denied, one must also deny any conclusions that depended on it; proofs must not retain consequences of a removed hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous justification for neglecting higher-order terms (product rule example)
rubrics_metrics.description: When taking increments of product AB the true increment is AB + aB + bA + ab; the common method drops ab as 'exceeding small' — such rejection requires justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When discarding 'ab' or other higher-order infinitesimals in derivations, provide principled justification (e.g., limiting argument, bounding error) showing the discarded term does not affect the claimed result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimacy of letting increments 'vanish' in series manipulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the Increments vanish; i.e. let the increments be nothing; the former supposition that the Increments were something is destroyed, and yet an Expression got by virtue thereof is retained — which is inconclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infinite-series or binomial expansions used with the device 'let the increment vanish' must demonstrate that passage to the limit preserves the relations derived under the nonzero increment assumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability and consistency of notation and signification
rubrics_metrics.description: Signs may be made to denote either any thing or nothing at all; but you must argue consistently with such its Signification, and not proceed upon a double Meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbols (e.g., x, dx, o) must carry the same intended meaning throughout a proof; do not covertly change the semantic status of a symbol mid-derivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence between algebraic expressions and geometric quantities
rubrics_metrics.description: Algebraical Expressions compared with Geometrical Quantities ... Correspondent Quantities Algebraical and Geometrical equated shewed not to obtain in Infinitesimals, but it must also obtain in finite quantities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When translating between algebraic species and geometric magnitudes, ensure the correspondence holds in the finite (assignable) case or otherwise justify why infinitesimal reasoning legitimately represents finite geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of operations on 'nothing' (division by zero and similar)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing is said that a finite Quantity divided by nothing is infinite — whether the common Assumption that a finite Quantity divided by nothing is infinite be not of this Number?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid manipulations that require treating 'nothing' (zero) as a quantity subject to regular arithmetic operations unless a rigorous limiting or algebraic framework justifies them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrations must proceed from principles, not from conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: In every other Science Men prove their Conclusions by their Principles, and not their Principles by the Conclusions. But if in yours you should allow your selves this unnatural way of proceeding, the Consequence would be that you must take up with Induction, and bid adieu to Demonstration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid circular reasoning or inferring foundational principles from the results they are supposed to justify; demonstration should be deductive from clear postulates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency in the ontological status of infinitesimals
rubrics_metrics.description: The notion or Idea of an infinitesimal Quantity ... as it an Object simply apprehended by the Mind, hath been already considered; yet the method of getting rid of such Quantities is done without the least formal demonstration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If infinitesimals are introduced, their ontological and logical status must be made explicit; if they are to be eliminated, exhibit a legitimate method (e.g., limit process) that removes them without invalid steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intelligibility of higher-order fluxions (second, third, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: A second Fluxion be inconceivable, what are we to think of third, fourth, fifth Fluxions, and so on without end?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a theory requires iterated fluxions/derivatives of arbitrarily high order, provide account that makes such higher-order entities intelligible or avoid invoking them where they are not conceptually warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of propagated errors from premises to conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever errors are admitted in the Premises, proportional errors ought to be apprehended in the Conclusion, be they finite or infinitesimal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track how approximations or neglected terms affect conclusions; show discarded terms do not introduce errors that invalidate the final result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid relying on prestige or implicit deference to authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Men submit to your Decisions where you have no right to decide, and that this is one short way of making an informed Infidel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematical acceptance should rest on reasoned demonstration rather than deference to celebrated authors or authority of style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform application of logical rules across algebra and geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Rules of Logic do not obtain in both Cases? And whether we have not right to expect and demand the same Evidence in both?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same standards of rigor and evidential support in algebraic manipulations (species/notations) as in geometric demonstrations; do not permit laxity in one domain that is disallowed in the other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish series/notations of velocities vs nascent increments
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a Series, of mere Velocities, or of mere nascent Increments, corresponding thereunto, be as easily conserved?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a series representation is used, specify whether its terms represent velocities, increments, or other quantities, and keep that interpretation consistent when manipulating or summing the series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation in diagrams must match intended generality
rubrics_metrics.description: When diagrams are general Substitutes or Representatives, it doth not follow that we may not limit or consider the number of Parts into which such particular Lines are divisible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise care when using geometric diagrams as universal representatives; explicitly state whether you are treating a diagram as symbolic of all assignable magnitudes or as a specific finite figure with limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer intelligible, consistent postulates over apparent accuracy by sophism
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it would not be righter to approximate fairly, than to endeavour at Accuracy by Sophisms? Whether it would not be more decent to proceed by Trials and Inductions, than to pretend to demonstrate by false Principles?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor methods with transparent, consistent premises (even if approximate) over methods that claim exactness but rely on obscurities or fallacious maneuvers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit the 'shifting of the hypothesis' fallacy (suppositio fallax)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Shifting of the Hypothesis, or (as we may call it) the fallacia Suppositionis be not a Sophism, that far and wide infects the modern Reasonings?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not change the hypothesis mid-proof (e.g., assume increments nonzero to compute, then assume zero and keep prior derived relations). Proofs must be internally consistent in their suppositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require metaphysical/ontological clarity for primitive notions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Extension can be supposed an Attribute of a Being Immutable and eternal? Whether Motion can be conceived in Point of Space? And if Motion cannot, whether Velocity can?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify the underlying metaphysical assumptions about extension, divisibility, motion, and velocity when they are used as primitive notions in analysis; ambiguous metaphysics undermines logical foundations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretability of algebraic symbols at beginning and end of arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an Algebraist ... can expect indulgence for obscure Principles or incorrect Reasonings? And whether an Algebraical Note or Species can at the end of a Process be interpreted in a Sense, which could not have been substituted for it at the beginning?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbols and algebraic species should be interpretable in the same way at every stage; final re-interpretations that were not legitimate at the outset are unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Care when narrowing general reasoning to particular cases
rubrics_metrics.description: When you limit them to stand for particular things, you do not limit yourself to reason consistently with the Nature of such particular things?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When passing from general symbolic reasoning to particular numerical or geometric instantiations, ensure the specialized reasoning obeys constraints of the particular case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical methods should cultivate genuine understanding, not only computational facility
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether tedious Calculations in Algebra and Fluxions be the likeliest Method to improve the Mind? And whether Mens being accustomed to reason altogether about Mathematical Signs and Figures, doth not make them at a loss how to reason without them?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer methods that promote conceptual clarity and rigorous reasoning rather than merely training in formal manipulations detached from intelligible foundations.
